details:
I would like to make it possible to implement audio middleware Such as FMOD and Wwise, with their codebase for Unity, Into VR chat.

 With audio middleware, it is possible to implement sounds and specializations in more versatile means than the ONSP allows for.  Furthermore, you could have much more parameter driven options for audio attenuation, audio progression, and even audio triggering. 

Example 1. Suppose you designed a world Where there was a monster you had to go kill.   You only knew where he was by the sound of his roar.... with middleware, you can Set parameters for that sound effect To play with certain attenuation based on each avatars distance from the monster.  You could also set it so that a completely different file Plays based On where that monster maybe or what they might be doing

Example 2.   Suppose you had 2D  Music playing in the background as your party progressed to find this monster. Certain factors can come into play such as stress, or even your health. With middleware, You could make the music you’re playing adaptive to parameter changes in your game environment. You could set it so that it played a softer motif When the stress the situation was low and that monster was not around, but then once the monster came into proximity, the music could then seamlessly transition over into a different music track with higher tempos or dynamics.  

You could even make it possible to trigger sounds based on being picked up, being interacted with, all manner of sound as it relates to your VR chat world.  

 Example 3. Suppose you wanted to allow players to have weapons which shot at that monster ( guns, weapons, rocket launchers, explosives),  you could not only implement those sound affects against others, but you can also create mixer groups which allow for you to balance sounds based on that environment.  You shoot a gun, set off an explosion, die, gain an achievement,  complete a quest, and you can set up a side chain which ducks out the music and the sounds around you to drawl the players attention to the Sounds in a mixer group With the compressor on it

Example 4.  Suppose the player walks out of a room in a building in your world. On the inside of that room  you might hear the sound of two  Nonplayer characters talking as you would in a normal setting, but when you step out of that room, you hear the sound reverberating in different directions, sounding a little bit more muffled. With audio middleware such as Wwise, you can set up reverb zones in each of the rooms Which reflect how the sound travels, based on the materials of the objects occluding the sound and reflecting it.

With the ONSP however, there Isn’t very much versatility with regards to implementing and manipulating sounds.  You just drag an audio object into the hierarchy,  and it automatically is set to be three-dimensional when you build the world. There’s nothing that tells it to be triggered on a certain action in the audio source in the inspector. It’s just a floating audio object with no real functionality, no adaptability, No interactivity.

If there was a way to integrate middleware into these worlds for one particular reason… There is nothing regarding headset relation on which to attach a middleware audio listener. Middleware listeners reference audio banks from their respective middleware project banks.  So if you have a middleware project, you could reference that bank, and rather  then having to attach individual audio objects into the game from your assets folder, you would have an entire array of sounds and music organized and at your fingertips, with each of its parameters automatically generated for your game. 

 As a world developer in training, I believe this would be very useful thing to have. So if you could please either make VR chat compatible with a piece of middleware, or even tell me how to attach an audio listener to avatars as they generate and spawn into a world, That would be most helpful.
title: Make Audio middleware integration comSo if you have a projectpatible with VR Chat
